content.intro: This lesson develops topic 193 of the supplied curriculum: **NumPy and pandas**. The main starting point is **Converting between arrays and Series**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Scientific Python tools share ndarray data, but each library has its own contract. Check shape, dtype, mutability, missing values, and conversion/copy behavior at boundaries.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **NumPy and pandas** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Converting between arrays and Series** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a downstream library never copies or converts
common_mistakes.why: Boundary adapters can coerce dtype or allocate new arrays.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the receiving library's documented conversion and mutability behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a NumPy array as a generic tensor everywhere
common_mistakes.why: Array libraries can differ in device, dtype, and operation semantics.
common_mistakes.fix: Document conversions and validate shapes and types at the boundary.
